title: Observability: adaptive IO stripes and OTEL context broker
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: recent incidents and micro-benchmarks show that the observability hot-path incurs high syscalls and unpredictable tail latency when the span/log export path is under load. This ticket implements two coordinated refactors: (1) an 'adaptive IO stripes' background writer that shards export work across a configurable set of single-threaded writers to reduce contention and syscalls; and (2) a lightweight OTEL context broker process that centralizes context propagation and sampling decisions to avoid repeated expensive context reconstruction in hot request paths. Both changes aim to reduce p50/p95 tokenized-request latencies and cut CPU/time spent in serialization and syscall-backed log flushes.
rationale: We have repeated performance regressions during sudden traffic spikes driven by the synchronous flush path and high-cardinality label handling. Previous approaches (single shared writer + heavier per-request sampling) produced lock contention and memory churn. The adaptive IO stripes approach minimizes cross-thread locks and staggers flushes; the OTEL context broker replaces ad-hoc, per-request sampling logic with a compact in-memory decision cache, decreasing allocations and enabling consistent sampling across routes.
tech_notes:
PoC implemented in runtime-agent v2.2 branch. Key design points:
- Introduce N writer stripes (default 4) where each stripe owns a ring-buffer of export envelopes; producers push with a cheap CAS and backpressure metric.
- Stripe selection: fast-consistent-hash(req.trace_id) to keep KV cache locality for hot traces.
- Broker: a small gRPC/UDS service (co-located) that accepts context attach/detach and returns a 16-byte sampling token and small decision flags; uses a 64K-entry LRU with TTL.
- Fallback: if broker unavailable, siloed process falls back to local deterministic sampling (same algorithm as broker) and increments a broker-miss metric.
- Memory: preallocate envelopes and reuse via pool to avoid GC spikes.
- Metrics: per-stripe queue depth, enqueue latency histogram, broker_miss_ratio, broker_request_latency.
acceptance_criteria:
- No regression in p50 latency on synthetic production-like load.
- p95 improved by at least 12% for observability-heavy endpoints in canary (internal benchmark).
- Exporter CPU usage reduced by >= 20% in benchmark.
- Fallback path exercised in test harness and broker_miss_ratio < 1% in canary.
- Automated e2e smoke (tracing continuity) passing in staging.
- Code review sign-offs from infra and observability leads.
implementation_steps:
1) Create stripe writer library and integrate into agent exporter (feature flagged).
2) Implement context broker service with in-memory LRU and test harness.
3) Wire runtime to call broker attach/detach in the hot path with optimized fast-path.
4) Add metrics and dashboards.
5) Canary rollout to 5% runtime fleet, monitor, iterate.
6) Ramp to 25% then 100% after SLO checks.
7) Deprecate legacy per-request sampling shim after full rollout.
rollout_plan:
Phase A: Feature flag off, run smoke tests in staging (1 day).
Phase B: Canary 5% for 48h with alert thresholds: broker_miss_ratio > 2% or stripe_queue_depth > 95th percentile alerts.
Phase C: If no regressions, 25% for 72h, then full rollout.
Rollback: flip feature flag or scale broker replica down and let clients fallback to deterministic sampling.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: stripe enqueue/dequeue correctness, broker LRU TTL eviction.
- Integration: simulate 50k RPS synthetic tracing load, assert enqueue success rate and stable latencies.
- Chaos: kill broker process, ensure fallback path observed and no request failures.
- Benchmark: measure CPU and allocation profile before/after with linux perf and go pprof (attached).
open_questions:
- Default stripe count: 4 or 8? Quick bench suggests diminishing returns beyond 6.
- Broker placement: sidecar vs shared host process; current PoC uses shared process per host for lower memory.
- Should sampling control be exposed to Console as a rollout knob? Product input needed.
